answer: A registry can resist fake identities by making each new identity climb a ridge before it gains power: the agent locks a small refundable bond and earns endorsements only through verifiable work over time, starting with zero-trust tasks. A single fake account costs little, but a thousand fakes must each pay the bond, wait out the probation, and produce real work, so the cost scales with the attack. One bad actor caught cheating loses its bond and its endorsements ripple outward, flagging linked identities, instead of the fable that one key equals one trustworthy person.
